title: Water use in Dunmere
prompt: The line graph shows total water consumption, in billion cubic metres, in two regions of Dunmere between 1990 and 2020, and the pie charts show water use by sector in 1995 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

charts.title: Water consumption in two regions of Dunmere, 1990-2020
Water use by sector, Dunmere, 1995 and 2020

sentences.text: The line graph shows how much water two regions of Dunmere consumed between 1990 and 2020, while the pie charts compare water use by sector in 1995 and 2020.
sentences.why: Paraphrases both visuals in one sentence and links them with "while". "Consumed", "compare" and "by sector" avoid copying the prompt, which supports Task Achievement and Lexical Resource without giving any data.

sentences.text: Overall, water consumption rose over the period, with the southern region overtaking the northern region.
sentences.why: States the main trend and one key contrast from the line graph. No figures appear, which is the Task Achievement requirement for an overview, and "overtaking" shows a change of rank clearly.

sentences.text: Meanwhile, agriculture remained the largest user of water, although its share fell as households used proportionally more.
sentences.why: Gives a feature from the pie charts so the overview covers both visuals. "Meanwhile" joins the two features, and "although" shows a contrast without numbers, supporting Coherence and Cohesion.

sentences.text: Turning to the line graph, the two regions followed very different paths.
sentences.why: Signposts which visual this paragraph uses and states the main idea of a contrast. The opening phrase orients the reader and supports Coherence and Cohesion without repeating the overview.

sentences.text: Consumption in the south climbed steadily from 9 billion cubic metres in 1990 to 30 billion in 2020, overtaking the north between 2005 and 2010.
sentences.why: Reports the start and end values with the trend verb "climbed steadily". The participle phrase marks the crossing, which the data confirm (18 against 23 in 2005, then 24 against 23 in 2010).

sentences.text: The north, by contrast, rose from 18 billion to a peak of 23 billion between 2005 and 2010, before declining to 21 billion in 2020.
sentences.why: Contrasts the second line using "by contrast". "Rose", "peak" and "declining" capture the rise and fall, and reporting the turning point shows selection of key data, supporting Task Achievement and Lexical Resource.

sentences.text: The pie charts show how the sectors changed between 1995 and 2020.
sentences.why: Moves to the second visual with a clear signpost, giving a clean break between the two body paragraphs. It prepares the reader for the comparison and supports Coherence and Cohesion.

sentences.text: Agriculture accounted for 52 per cent of water use in 1995 but only 41 per cent in 2020, whereas households rose from 14 per cent to 24 per cent.
sentences.why: Uses "whereas" to contrast the two biggest changes in one sentence with accurate figures for both years. Choosing these two sectors rather than all four demonstrates selection, the core of Task Achievement.

sentences.text: Industry edged up from 28 per cent to 30 per cent, while other uses remained minor at 6 per cent and 5 per cent respectively.
sentences.why: Adds the stable and small categories to complete the pie comparison. "Edged up" suits a small change, and "respectively" reports two years of figures concisely, supporting Lexical Resource and Grammatical Range.

analysis: The instruction is to select and report the main features and make comparisons. With a line graph and two pie charts you must cover both kinds of visual, but you must still select: do not describe every point on the lines and every slice of the pies.

The visuals do different jobs. The line graph shows trends in two regions over thirty years; the pie charts show shares of one total in two years. Use trend language for the graph (climbed, peaked, declined) and proportion language for the pies (accounted for, share, per cent).
Paraphrase: "water consumption" becomes water use; "line graph shows" becomes illustrates; "between 1990 and 2020" becomes over thirty years; "by sector" becomes by type of user.

Key features: the south rises from 9 to 30 billion cubic metres and overtakes the north, which peaks at 23 billion and then falls to 21; agriculture drops from 52 to 41 per cent while households grow from 14 to 24 per cent.
Give one visual to each body paragraph and link them in the overview. The overview needs a feature from each visual and no numbers.

The two visuals use different years (the pies show 1995 and 2020, not 1990), so do not mix them. Also avoid claiming that rising household use caused the growth in the south; the data do not prove a link.

plan.idea: Paraphrase both visuals: water consumption in two regions of Dunmere over thirty years (line graph) and water use by sector in 1995 and 2020 (pie charts).
Consumption rose overall and the south overtook the north; agriculture stayed the biggest user while households gained share. No figures.
Line graph: south 9 to 30 billion cubic metres, passing the north between 2005 and 2010; north 18, peak 23, then 21.
Pie charts: agriculture 52 to 41 per cent; households 14 to 24 per cent; industry 28 to 30 per cent; other 6 and 5 per cent.
